title: A5's manager rings again, 9 days after the complaint call, and nobody answers
purpose: Story S1. One of the three unanswered calls from Wade Carlisle's number in the nine days after call 17. No recording, no transcript and no verdict: the call log's legs and a missed_call row that stays waiting. It is older than the callback queue's seven days at T, so it is on no screen and is found by a query (question S1.5); it has no person, only the desk it rang first (question S1.6).

call.day: 9 calendar days after call 17, which is on the Tuesday of week T-19 (rule R6; card S01, call 20)
call.note: Central time, inside opening hours. The public line rings one desk for 20 s, then every desk for 15 s (calls/DESIGN.md section 2).

scenario.who_calls: Wade Carlisle, operations manager of company account A5, waiting for the call back promised in call 17.
scenario.what_happens: The line rings out. He leaves no message; the seed has no voicemail.

facts.note: Ledger s1.a5: three misses 1, 6 and 9 calendar days after the complaint call, first desks 302, 303, 302; no answered call to or from the number afterwards.

missed_call.why_not_on_screen: the queue shows seven days; this miss is months old

truth.note: Nobody answered and nobody called back. A missed call has no person: the data gives the desk it rang first and who was rostered, not who missed it.

why.verdict: None: an unanswered call has no recording, no transcript and no scorecard row.

new_facts: The time of this miss: 16:15 Central on its day; 35 seconds of ringing; the first desk 302, then desks 301, 302 and 303 together.
